subject: Production regression: Quantis Labs - elevated latency & errors (commercial options)
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara@quantislabs.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@quantislabs.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in errors/latency impacting batch jobs

Evelyn,

We started seeing a sustained increase in latency and error rates against the Redwood endpoint serving our nightly batch ingestion starting around 22:30 UTC on Jul 7. Over the last 10 hours we've had multiple job failures and timeouts — average tail latency jumped from ~120ms to >2.5s and the error rate climbed to ~4.6% for POST /v1/generate. This is material for our nightly processing and has blocked downstream analytics jobs.

Examples:
- 2027-07-08T03:12:13Z - HTTP 500 - "internal server error" - 2.8s
- 2027-07-08T04:05:47Z - HTTP 504 - upstream timeout - 3.1s
- 2027-07-08T06:42:01Z - batch job failed after retrying 5 times

We escalated on our side, and would like an urgent remediation plan and a commercial remediation discussion (credits/invoice adjustments) per our SLA section 6. Please advise next steps and availability for a call in the next 2 hours. We're in PST.

Attachments: sample_errors.log (text)

Thanks,
Sara Kim
Director of Platform Engineering
Quantis Labs

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara@quantislabs.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in errors/latency impacting batch jobs

Sara —

I'm very sorry for the disruption. Thank you for the concrete examples and timestamps — that's exactly what we need.

Immediate items we've put in motion:
- Dylan's team is running a full investigation and has kicked off remediation playbooks.
- We've routed your production traffic to a mitigated path to reduce tail latency while the root cause is diagnosed.
- I've scheduled a 10:00 AM PST call to walk through what we've seen and next steps.

For the commercial side: I understand you expect the standard SLA remedies; I will coordinate with Sales and Legal and bring a proposal to the call. I've attached a short incident summary (incident_report.pdf) with the initial observations.

10:00 AM PST call details: Zoom (link in calendar invite) — please confirm if that works.

Again, apologies. We're treating this as priority.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.Hart@redwood.com
Attachment: incident_report.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Sara Kim <sara@quantislabs.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@quantislabs.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in errors/latency impacting batch jobs

Folks — quick technical note and recommended commercial starting point for discussion.

What we know (initial):
- Root cause: regression in autoscaler behavior caused by a recent config change in the request batching heuristics. Under the specific Quantis traffic mix (long sequences + bursty throughput) certain GPU pools were starved and fell back to CPU paths leading to >2s tail latencies and elevated 5xx.
- Mitigation: rolled back the heuristic change at 08:55 PDT, and applied temporary capacity reallocation to the affected pool. Synthetic checks are green and Quantis's sampled traffic shows latency returning to baseline over the last 15 minutes.
- Impact window (preliminary): Jul 7 22:30 UTC -> Jul 8 08:55 UTC (~10.5 hours). We are continuing to refine the impacted window and token counts.

Commercial calc (proposal):
- Per SLA section 6.2, service credits are proportional to outage duration within the billing period. For a ~10.5 hour window where the agreed availability target was missed, preliminary credit would be the prorated percentage of monthly invoice. I've attached a simple workbook (proposed_credit_calc.xlsx) with three scenarios: conservative (standard SLA formula), enhanced (goodwill extra), and full-make-whole (exec-level).

Recommended next steps for the call:
1) Confirm final impacted window and token counts (we will provide a definitive CSV by EOD).
2) Present the three credit scenarios and trade-offs (time-to-settlement vs. amount).
3) If Quantis prefers an enhanced commercial path, propose a one-page amendment for signatures.

Happy to walk through the workbook on the call.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_credit_calc.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara@quantislabs.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@quantislabs.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in errors/latency impacting batch jobs

Sara / Liam —

First, my apologies — this should not have happened. I appreciate the clear examples and your patience while our team sorted the root cause. I want to offer a couple of concrete commercial paths so we can close this out quickly and get you back to baseline with confidence: 

Option A — Standard SLA credit (fast):
- Apply the standard SLA credit calculated per section 6.2 of the contract. Estimated at ~12% of your monthly invoice for the impacted billing period (final % to be confirmed after token reconciliation). Settlement via invoice credit; minimal paperwork; can complete in 7–10 business days.

Option B — Enhanced commercial goodwill (preferred for faster resolution + extra support):
- One-time commercial credit of $40,000 applied to your next invoice + 3 months of prioritized SRE support (two named on-call rotations and weekly rollout reviews).
- If you want a formal amendment, we can execute a one-page addendum; otherwise, we can process the credit as a billing adjustment.

Option C — Make-whole & executive support (for escalated enterprise risk):
- Larger credit and timeline commitments; requires legal amendment and exec sign-off (we can fast-track if needed).

I'm flexible on the structure — the choices trade time-to-settlement and amount. If you prefer quick closure, Option B is usually what customers pick.

I'll also put a single-line HubSpot note and link to JIRA-INF-3198 for our internal trace.

Can you confirm which option you prefer? If you'd like us to draft the one-page amendment, we'll circulate it this afternoon.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
Zoom: 10:00 AM PST notes appended
Related: https://hubspot.example/contacts/hs_12345, JIRA-INF-3198

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@quantislabs.com>

Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in errors/latency impacting batch jobs

Vivek, Evelyn — thanks for the transparency and for moving quickly.

Quantis prefers Option B (enhanced goodwill): $40,000 credit + 3 months prioritized SRE support. We'll accept that in principle. Two quick asks before we finalize:
1) Please provide a one-page confirmation/letter with the credit amount, how it will appear on our next invoice, and the effective dates for the 3 months of prioritized SRE support.
2) Please share the final token reconciliation CSV and a short summary of root cause analysis by EOD tomorrow — our procurement/legal team needs that to close the amendment.

If you can send the confirmation and the draft amendment, we'll loop Legal for a quick signature cycle. We can also schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review mitigations and testing plans.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Engineering
Quantis Labs
